### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c56115bf962cb301fb046c54680620d37e5ab2fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `69459504060ff760f072257b064a5882ead74c0e` — the merge of head `0d4ea3e5b0f7e2109f5dc661b1ea02aede4c7acd` into base `c56115bf962cb301fb046c54680620d37e5ab2fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 69459504060ff760f072257b064a5882ead74c0e && git checkout 69459504060ff760f072257b064a5882ead74c0e

git fetch origin c56115bf962cb301fb046c54680620d37e5ab2fb 0d4ea3e5b0f7e2109f5dc661b1ea02aede4c7acd && git checkout -B drift-repro c56115bf962cb301fb046c54680620d37e5ab2fb && git merge --no-ff 0d4ea3e5b0f7e2109f5dc661b1ea02aede4c7acd
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0d4ea3e5b0f7e2109f5dc661b1ea02aede4c7acd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-batch-blank-id.test.ts + packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (the per-base-path registrar loop at 4796, the environment-scoped twin), packages/metadata-core/src/engine-update-dispatch.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-delete-dispatch.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the update dispatch at 16854 and the delete dispatch at 19900), packages/spec/src/api/batch.zod.ts (CrossObjectBatchOperationSchema, CrossObjectBatchRequestSchema, DeleteManyRequestSchema), packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (rowRequiredIdError at 16714/16786/17277, deleteManyData at 17391), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts, packages/rest/package.json, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (WHICH LEVEL), .changeset/config.json, .changeset/pre.json, .claude/agents/os-dev.md (the bounded in-place-fix exemption); prose face .changeset/24781-rest-batch-blank-id-400.md

### ① Derived judgments

**Gate state at render** (latest run per name on the head, 40 names).
- 34 completed `success` or `skipped`. Green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, every Lint and Type Check lane (the scoped `query-options erasure` lane included), and the claim and issue guards.
- **`Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)` are `in_progress`: NOT MEASURED**, never a pass. The dev's local run (305 files, 6144 tests) is the implementation claim, not the gate.
- Judged on the diff.

**Net diff vs `main`** (`c56115bf9`, merge base `307ce4c4b`): 3 files, +280/-7. No governed surface. The head repo is the base repo. Far under 3,000 lines.

**The door and its twin.** `registerBatchEndpoints(bp)` runs once per base path (`rest-server.ts:4796`). So `POST /api/v1/batch` and `POST /api/v1/environments/:environmentId/batch` are one handler, and `isScoped` changes only how `environmentId` is read. Both mounts move together. Right.

**The new rule, read against the engine.**
- `batchOpRowAddress`: update reads `op.id ?? data?.id`, and delete reads `op.id`. These are byte-identical to the expressions the two write arms already used (`const id = op.id ?? data?.id`; `where: { id: op.id }`). Both arms now call the helper, so the check and the arm cannot diverge.
- `namesNoRow` asks `resolveEngineUpdateDispatch({ id }, undefined)` / `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch({ where: { id } })` whether `kind !== 'by-id'`. Those are the functions `ObjectQL.update` (`engine.ts:16854`) and `ObjectQL.delete` (`engine.ts:19900`) dispatch on, exported from `@objectstack/metadata-core`'s index.
- The batch arms pass no `where` and no `multi`. So for these calls the engine's only non-`reject` outcome is `by-id`, which is a truthy `string` / `number` / `bigint` (`asScalarId`, `scalarDeleteId`, then `if (id)`).
- Every address the check now refuses is therefore one the engine would have thrown on (`… requires an ID or options.multi=true`) inside the atomic transaction. The batch rolled back and answered 5xx.
- **No request that answered 2xx or wrote a row before is refused now.** That holds by construction, not only by the pins.
- `@objectstack/metadata-core` is already a `dependencies` entry of `@objectstack/rest`, imported by six other rest source files. No new package edge.

**The PR body's `## Contract` table, row by row:**
- **update, `"id": ""`**: was 500 `DATABASE_ERROR`, now the missing-id 400. Right. The card measured the 500, and `""` is a falsy scalar, never by-id.
- **update, no `id`, `data.id` in `""` / `0` / `false` / `true` / `{}` / `[]`**: right. `asScalarId` yields `undefined` for the non-scalars, and the falsy scalars fail `if (id)`. Before, each reached the engine and was rejected.
- **update, `"id": ""` beside a real `data.id`**: right. `""` is not nullish, so `??` keeps it in the check and in the arm alike.
- **delete, `"id": ""`, with or without `data.id`**: was 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, now the 400. Right. Delete reads `id` alone, and `""` is falsy.
- **delete, no `id`, the id only in `data.id`**: was 400 `INVALID_FILTER`, now 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Right.
  - The old check passed on `op.data?.id`, and the arm then sent `where: { id: undefined }`.
  - The spec's filter-comparand guard refuses an `undefined` comparand before dispatch (`scalarDeleteId` would reject after it), so nothing was ever deleted through `data.id`.
  - This is a code change on an already-refused shape, and it is named honestly.
- **"a later step used to answer first"**: right. The id loop sits where it always did, on `main` and on the head alike: after `enforceBatchSize`, and before `loadObjectItems` / `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` and the transaction. A blank id now takes the path a missing id already took.

**The unchanged list.** Every item is right:
- a missing or `null` id → the same 400 (`null` is not a scalar);
- a real id, by `id` or `data.id` (update) or by `id` (delete) → by-id, with the arms unchanged;
- `data.id: { $ref: n }` → `isBatchRef` is the old inline predicate verbatim (`v && typeof v === 'object' && '$ref' in v`), so the check skips it, and the in-transaction resolver still refuses an unresolvable one with `BATCH_UNRESOLVED_REF`;
- unknown and whitespace ids → truthy strings, by-id, and the engine answers 404;
- `atomic: false` → `BATCH_NOT_ATOMIC` precedes the loop, and an omitted `atomic` defaults to `true` in the schema;
- `op.id` is `z.string().optional()`, so a non-string `id` gets the schema's 400 first.

**Other doors.** Both are right and untouched by the diff:
- The per-object `batchData` rows refuse on `if (!record.id) throw rowRequiredIdError(...)` (`protocol.ts:16714`, `:16786`, and update again at `:17277`). That is a falsy test, so `""` is refused per row.
- `deleteManyData`'s `isScalarId` admits a string only when it is non-empty, so `ids: [""]` answers 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`.
- `@objectstack/runtime` has no twin to fix: `http-dispatcher.ts:2263` reports `transactionalBatch: { enabled: false }`, and `domains/data.ts` mounts no `/batch`.

**Public surface.**
- `batch-routes.ts` still exports only `BatchRouteHost` and `registerBatchEndpoints`. The three helpers are module-private.
- No spec, export, type or stored shape moves. The accept-set change is confined to the one door (two mounts).

**Pins.**
- 11 refusal rows assert the whole `{ status, body }`, that `engine.transaction` is never called, and that the seeded row is unchanged.
- One row pins that an earlier `create` is not written, and 8 controls cover the rest.
- They were red on `main` (12 failed, 8 passed), and the two ablations were restored hash-equal.
- That is the pin shape the card asked for: status, `code`, and the engine never called.
- The test imports are package imports of declared rest devDependencies (92 rest tests already boot `@objectstack/driver-sql`), with no cross-package path read.

Noted, not a verdict item: `CrossObjectBatchOp` restates the spec's `CrossObjectBatchOperationParsed` by hand. It names the inline literal the old line already carried, with the same shape.

### ② Semver level

**The changeset is right on all three axes.** `.changeset/24781-rest-batch-blank-id-400.md` carries:
- `'@objectstack/rest': minor`, with a `**BREAKING**` banner;
- the adr-0087 comment marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`;
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the same line the PR body carries.

**Level.**
- The tree is in pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`; rest is at `18.0.0-next.5`), and the launch-window convention of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` is the authority: a declared `narrowing` is BREAKING and ships `minor`.
- Its LEVEL axis enforces exactly that (`declaration.value === 'no'` with the `narrowing` arm → `enforce`). So the dispatched `patch` would have been refused, and `minor` is the only grade the gate admits.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: `success`.

**Disposition.**
- Nothing authorable, exported, typed or stored moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed.
- The changeset's FROM/TO lines describe wire answers (500 to 400), with the remedy "send the record's id". That is not a consumer-code or metadata rewrite, and `check-adr-0087-registration` admitted it.

**Prose.** It states the shipped behaviour truly. The banner's "No request that succeeded before is refused now" is the ① invariant, and the whitespace-id, per-object-door and ordering sentences each match the cited code.

`skip-changeset` does not apply: a released package moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **"Changeset graded `minor`, not the dispatched `patch`."** Answered, right: see ②. The dispatch's `patch` contradicts the narrowing line the same dispatch wrote, and the gate decides.
2. **"A delete addressed only by `data.id`, fixed in place under the bounded exemption."** Answered, accepted. `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` sets four conditions, all required, and each holds:
   - It is the card's own defect class: the up-front check passing an op that its arm then sends with no address, on the identical line.
   - It is mechanical and pinned: one rule, `namesNoRow(batchOpRowAddress(...))`, and REFUSED row 11, red on `main` as 400 `INVALID_FILTER`.
   - No other claim is on the file: the claim's serial read found no open PR touching `batch-routes.ts`.
   - It is the same gate family with no new verification surface: the same `local` vitest project, and one test file beside `rest-batch-endpoint.test.ts`.

   The two debts are paid. The file surface was already the claim's (`batch-routes.ts`, nothing to supplement), and the PR body names the fix with evidence. The dispatch's own "one rule serves both … fixed in the same rule and named in the PR body" says the same.
3. **"`atomic: false` is refused `BATCH_NOT_ATOMIC` before the id check."** Answered, verified in code. The rule holds for `atomic: true` and for `atomic` omitted.
4. **"Merged `origin/main` `307ce4c4b` before opening."** AGENTS.md §10. The head is that merge, and the net diff is exactly the three files. Accepted.
5. **"Model-free commit trailers" and "worktree cleaned".** Housekeeping per AGENTS.md. Nothing for this record.
6. **Out-of-scope finding, carrier `#24768`.** The engine's `… requires an ID` throws still answer 500 for other callers, and `DATABASE_ERROR` and `INTERNAL_ERROR` disagree between the verbs. Holding it off is right: the dispatch named it a hold-off, and the carrier is open. Not escalated.
7. **Acceptance note: `CrossObjectBatchOperationSchema.id` carries no `.min(1)`.** Not filing it is right, for three reasons:
   - `packages/spec/**` was held off.
   - A schema `.min(1)` could never reach `data.id` (`0`, `false`, `{}`) anyway.
   - After this fix a blank `id` is refused at the door, so the schema's permissiveness is not a defect.

   No carrier is owed.

**Landing** stays the owning seat's. This PASS arms nothing: the six `Test Core` shards must conclude `success`, and the claim's main-red hold (`#24780`) governs the queue.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24781-batch-empty-id-400`
Reviewed-by: `session_01LmjU2x1faLZ39DVTFyVca6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
